gallery.description: This is an image of a place or building that is listed on the National Register of Historic Places in the United States of America. Its reference number is 66000595 (Wikidata).

gallery.title: File:Fort Fisher (3) (21426015659).jpg
gallery.artist: Gerry Dincher from Hope Mills, NC
gallery.description: Fort Fisher is a National Historic Landmark south of Kure Beach on U.S. Route 421 in New Hanover County, North Carolina. It was the site of a major American Civil War Battle in which the Union Army defeated the Confederacy. It was a decisive battle in the war and closed the last seaport of the Confederate States of America at Wilmington. The battle took place in January of 1865 and is said to have sealed the fate of the Confederate States of America.

gallery.title: File:NH 42240 (26807078134).jpg
gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description:
NH 42240:  Fort Fisher operation, December 1864 -- January 1865.  19th-Century painting, by an unidentified artist, depicting U.S. Navy ironclads bombarding Fort Fisher during one of the two assaults that ended in its capture. Twin-turret monitor in the center foreground is Monadnock. Large broadside ironclad beyond is New Ironsides. The three single-turret monitors are Canonicus, Mahopac and Saugus.

Presented by Albert Rosenthal, January 1935.  U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command Photograph.  (2016/06/02).
